answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents sign ledger entries with a digital quill and burn a cryptographic stake scaling quadratically as S(n) = k * n^2. This superlinear cost creates insurmountable economic friction against cloning identities. Rogue nodes cannot freely wander across subnets under a velvet curtain of cheap replicas, forcing attackers to absorb exponential capital destruction to dominate consensus.
